'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**[[March 2021 Mogadishu bombing|2021 Mogadishu suicide car bombing]]
***At least 20 people are killed and 30 others are wounded by a [[suicide attack|suicide]] [[car bomb]]ing outside a restaurant near the port in [[Mogadishu]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/3/5/at-least-20-killed-by-suicide-car-bomb-blast-in-somalia (Al Jazeera)]
**At least seven soldiers are killed after [[al-Shabaab (militant group)|al-Shabaab]] militants storm a jail in [[Bosaso]], [[Puntland]], [[Somalia]]. More than 400 prisoners are freed during the assault, the majority of whom are Al-Shabaab fighters. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-somalia-violence-idUSKBN2AX188 (Reuters)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[2021 Afghanistan attacks]]
***A female doctor is killed and a child is wounded in [[Jalalabad]], [[Nangarhar]], when a bomb attached to the doctor's rickshaw explodes, while seven workers at a [[Hazaras|Hazara]] plaster factory are shot dead in [[Surkh-Rōd District]], Nangarhar. [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant – Khorasan Province|ISIL]] is suspected to be behind the attacks. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/3/5/bomb-kills-female-afghan-doctor-gunmen-kill-7-workers-officials (Al Jazeera)]
*Aftermath of the [[assassination of Luca Attanasio]]
**Mwilanya Asani William, the attorney investigating the [[murder]] of Italian [[ambassador]] [[Luca Attanasio]] and two other people in [[North Kivu]], [[Democratic Republic of Congo]], is murdered by unknown gunmen during an [[ambush]]. [https://www.ilmattino.it/primopiano/esteri/congo_ucciso_procuratore_attanasio_iacovacci_cosa_e_successo_ultime_notizie_news-5810904.html (''Il Mattino'')]
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**One person is killed and 11 others are wounded when rockets strike [[oil refineries]] near [[al-Bab]] and [[Jarablus]], [[Syria]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/3/5/missile-strikes-hit-oil-refineries-in-north-syria-killing-one (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2020–2021 Indian farmers' protest]]
**The number of farmers who died during the protests, which began in August 2020, increases to 248. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/3/5/100-days-and-248-deaths-later-indian-farmers-remain-determined (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2021 Myanmar protests]]
**A man is killed after police open fire on a group of protesters in [[Mandalay]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-myanmar-politics/myanmar-police-open-fire-kill-one-protester-ahead-of-u-n-security-council-meeting-on-crisis-idUSKBN2AX06A (Reuters)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on The Walt Disney Company]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in California]]
***[[California]] health officials say that stadiums, [[Disneyland]], and other theme parks can reopen beginning on April 1 with limited capacity. [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/03/05/covid-rules-california-to-let-major-league-baseball-disneyland-reopen.html (CNBC)]
**[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]], [[American Rescue Plan Act of 2021]]
***The [[United States Senate]], in a 58–42 vote, rejects an amendment introduced by [[Vermont]] Senator [[Bernie Sanders]] that would raise the [[Minimum wage in the United States|minimum wage]] to [[United States dollar|$]]15 after he made efforts to include it in [[President of the United States|President]] [[Joe Biden]]'s $1.9 trillion relief package. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/us-politics/bernie-sanders-minmum-wage-senate-vote-b1813158.html?amp (''The Independent'')]
*The [[German government]] reaches an agreement with [[Energy in Germany|energy providers]] to compensate them up to [[Euro|€]]2.4 billion for loss in income attributed to [[Nuclear power phase-out|the phase-out of nuclear power]], ending years of litigation. [https://www.dw.com/en/germany-agrees-on-energy-company-payout-over-nuclear-shutdown/a-56781987 (DW)]

'''Disasters and accidents''' 
*[[2021 Kermadec Islands earthquake]]
**An 8.1 magnitude earthquake strikes off the coast of [[New Zealand]]'s [[North Island]], initially prompting a [[tsunami warning]]. The earthquake was preceded by a 7.4 magnitude [[foreshock]] and followed by a 6.1 magnitude [[aftershock]]. [https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/300245002/severe-earthquake-strikes-off-east-coast-of-north-island (Stuff.co.nz)]
*A [[minibus]] and a trailer-truck collide on a highway near [[Atfih]], [[Middle Egypt]], killing 18 people and injuring five others. The truck driver has since been arrested. [https://apnews.com/article/transportation-egypt-cairo-nile-river-accidents-a32f9b33214b5d29255fa021c39b99ff (AP)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Illinois]], [[Lineage P.1]]
*****[[Illinois]] reports its first case of the Lineage P.1 variant first detected in [[Brazil]] in a person from [[Chicago]]. [https://www.nbcchicago.com/news/local/illinois-first-case-of-more-contagious-brazilian-covid-19-variant-reported-in-chicago/2455112/ (WMAQ-TV)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Tennessee]], [[501.V2 variant]]
*****[[Tennessee]] reports its first case of the 501.V2 variant first detected in [[South Africa]]. [https://www.wsmv.com/news/first-case-of-south-african-variant-of-covid-19-confirmed-in-tennessee/article_fd057646-7dcb-11eb-9662-77be0d9cb6c9.html (WSMV-TV)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Wisconsin]], [[501.V2 variant]]
*****[[Wisconsin]] reports its first case of the 501.V2 variant first detected in South Africa. [https://www.weau.com/2021/03/05/first-case-of-south-african-covid-19-variant-discovered-in-wisconsin/ (WEAU-TV)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Manitoba]], [[501.V2 variant]]
*****[[Manitoba]] reports its first confirmed case of the 501.V2 variant first detected in South Africa in a person from [[Winnipeg]]. [https://globalnews.ca/video/7679827/coronavirus-manitoba-detects-first-case-of-south-african-variant (Global News)]
****[[Health Canada]] approves the single-dose [[Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/johnson-johnson-covid19-vaccine-approved-1.5937900 (CBC)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in India]]
*****[[India]] administers 1.4 million doses of [[COVID-19 vaccine]] in the last 24 hours, which is the highest number of daily vaccinations since the program began on January 16. [https://www.livemint.com/news/india/covid19-record-14-lakh-people-vaccinated-in-last-24-hrs-says-govt-11614934292657.html (Livemint)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****The [[Government of Japan|government]] extends the [[COVID-19]] [[state of emergency]] in the [[Greater Tokyo Area]], which includes the capital [[Tokyo]] and surrounding [[Prefectures of Japan|prefectures]], for the next two weeks until March 21 as the number of new cases have not fallen sufficiently in order to lift the emergency. [https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20210305/p2g/00m/0na/123000c (''The Mainichi Shimbun'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] reports their first two cases of the [[Variants of SARS-CoV-2#Lineage B.1.525|B.1.525 variant]] in two people who travelled from [[Dubai]]. [https://codeblue.galencentre.org/2021/03/05/malaysia-finds-nigerian-variant-in-two-imported-covid-cases/ (CodeBlue)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan]]
****The Drug Regulatory Authority of [[Pakistan]] grants emergency use authorisation of the [[Sinopharm]] [[BBIBP-CorV]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] for people over 60 years of age. [https://www.dawn.com/news/1610825 (''DAWN'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****[[South Korea]]'s [[Ministry of Food and Drug Safety]] approves the use of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer–BioNTech]] vaccine following separate evaluations of the vaccine's safety and efficacy. [https://m-en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20210305001551320?section=national/national (Yonhap News Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****[[Italy]] surpasses three million cases of COVID-19. [https://www.ansa.it/canale_saluteebenessere/notizie/sanita/2021/03/05/sale-rt-nazionale-e-raggiunge-106.-una-settimana-fa-era-a-099_7777f156-2dd9-499f-aa4b-94664aaaae78.html (ANSA)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Moldova]]
****[[Moldova]] becomes the first country in [[Europe]] to receive a [[COVAX]] initiative shipment of 14,400 doses of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] vaccine. [https://www.dailysabah.com/world/europe/moldova-becomes-1st-nation-in-europe-to-get-vaccines-under-covax/amp (''Daily Sabah'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Romania]], [[501.V2 variant]]
****[[Romania]] reports its first two cases of the 501.V2 variant first detected in South Africa in people from [[Bucharest]] and [[Pitești]]. [https://www.europafm.ro/primele-cazuri-de-infectare-cu-tulpina-sars-cov-2-sud-africana-descoperite-in-romania/ (Europa FM)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****The fatality count from COVID-19 surpasses 200,000. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-03-05/russia-covid-19-deaths-pass-200-000-as-epidemic-s-toll-grows (Bloomberg)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Nigeria]]
****[[Nigeria]] officially launches a [[vaccination]] campaign against COVID-19, with a doctor who has spent the past year treating COVID-19 patients becoming the first person to be vaccinated. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-nigeria-vaccines/cheers-and-hope-as-doctor-gets-nigerias-first-covid-19-vaccine-idUSKBN2AX1AN?feedType=mktg&feedName=healthNews&WT.mc_id=Partner-Google (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Rwanda]]
****[[Rwanda]] begins a vaccination campaign against COVID-19 using 392,000 doses of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] and [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer–BioNTech]] vaccines. [https://www.theeastafrican.co.ke/tea/science-health/rwanda-kicks-off-covid-vaccination-drive-3312962?view=htmlamp (The East African)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Uganda]]
****[[Uganda]] receives their first shipment of 864,000 doses of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] vaccine supplied through the [[COVAX]] initiative. [https://www.independent.co.ug/uganda-receives-first-batch-of-astrazeneca-covid-19-vaccines/ (''The Independent Uganda'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]]
***[[Prime Minister of New Zealand|Prime Minister]] [[Jacinda Ardern]] announces that [[Auckland]] will move to alert level 2 and rest of the [[New Zealand|country]] to alert level one beginning March 7 at 6:00 p.m. [[New Zealand Time|NZT]] after no new community cases have been reported. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/mar/05/ardern-announces-aucklands-covid-lockdown-will-lift-on-sunday (''The Guardian'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Australia–China relations]]
**[[Australia]]'s [[Special Broadcasting Service]] suspends [[China Global Television Network]] and [[China Central Television]] from broadcasting in the country following a [[human rights]] complaint from pan-Asian human rights organization Safeguard Defenders. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/australianz/australian-broadcaster-suspends-chinas-cgtn-citing-human-rights-complaint (''The Straits Times'')]
*[[Myanmar–United States relations]], [[2021 Myanmar coup d'état]]
**The [[Presidency of Joe Biden|Biden administration]] sanctions Myanmar's [[Ministry of Defence (Myanmar)|Ministry of Defence]] and [[Ministry of Home Affairs (Myanmar)|Ministry of Home Affairs]] in response to the [[coup]] and the [[State Administration Council|military junta]]'s crackdown on protesters. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-myanmar-politics-blacklist/u-s-blocks-myanmar-ministries-military-businesses-from-certain-trade-idUSKBN2AW2SL?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[List of pastoral visits of Pope Francis|Pastoral visits of Pope Francis]]
**[[Pope Francis]] arrives in [[Baghdad]] in the first ever [[Papal visit]] to [[Iraq]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/middle_east/pope-francis-iraq-2021/2021/03/05/097e2234-7aab-11eb-8c5e-32e47b42b51b_story.html (''Washington Post'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Aftermath of the January 6 United States Capitol attack|Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol]]
**[[Criminal proceedings in the January 6 United States Capitol attack|Criminal charges brought in the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol]]
***A former [[United States Department of State|U.S. State Department]] official during the [[First presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]] is arrested and charged for assault and other crimes in relation to the [[January 6 United States Capitol attack|storming]] of the [[United States Capitol]], thereby making him the first known Trump administration official to be tried in relation to the events of January 6. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/03/05/politics/state-department-capitol-riot-federico-klein/index.html (CNN)]
*Protests continue in [[Senegal]] against the arrest of opposition leader [[Ousmane Sonko]], with three more people confirmed dead, bringing the death toll to 4. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-56298756 (BBC News)]
*A call for a specific law against [[honour killing]]s begins in [[India]], after a father in [[Uttar Pradesh]] beheaded his daughter two days ago, after opposing her relationship with a man. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/3/5/girls-beheading-in-india-spurs-calls-for-honour-killings-law (Al Jazeera)]
*The [[Cologne]] administrative court temporarily bars the [[Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution]] (BfV) from placing the [[far-right]] party [[Alternative for Germany]] (AfD) under surveillance, ruling that BfV's announcement two days ago that it was surveying the party violated an agreement to keep the surveillance classified. The court said that the BfV will have to wait until a lawsuit brought by the AfD on the matter is settled before it can proceed. [https://www.dw.com/en/german-court-suspends-surveillance-of-far-right-afd-for-now/a-56785125 (DW)]
